retraction_note: due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised (Retraction notice, PDF p.1; article DOI 10.1155/2022/7295833, retraction DOI 10.1155/2022/9830750). Empirical claims (Tables 1-2) are unusable for calibration; only the standard mathematical kernels are extracted, each flagged.

primitives.name: Ordinary least-squares normal equation (multiple linear regression coefficients)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The algorithm establishes a multiple linear regression matrix between the target prediction sample and the training sample
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: lambda_i: multiple linear regression coefficient vector [units of Y per unit of the corresponding X column; dimensionless if X and Y share units]; X: design matrix of training-sample features [feature units, e.g. pixel intensity or normalized pose coordinate]; Y: target vector [prediction-target units, same as the pixel/feature being predicted]; T: transpose operator [dimensionless]; (X^T X)^{-1}: inverse Gram matrix [1/(feature units)^2]; sigma_i: residual / random-disturbance replacement [Y units]. Dimensional check: X^T Y carries [X][Y], (X^T X)^{-1} carries 1/[X]^2, product carries [Y]/[X] = lambda units; homogeneous. Source eq (14), with eq (13) the regression matrix and sigma_i the residuals.
primitives.assumptions: Linear model between target prediction sample and training sample; X has full column rank so X^T X is invertible; residuals sigma_i treated as the approximate replacement of the random disturbance term; three characteristic pixels used as prediction samples with their connected pixels as training samples (p.6). RETRACTED SOURCE: the journal retracted this article 'due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised' (Retraction notice, PDF p.1; Hindawi Research Integrity investigation). The mathematical kernels below are standard, durable formulas that survive the retraction, but the paper's empirical claims (Tables 1-2, ~80-97% accuracy) are NOT trustworthy and must never calibrate a model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: X^T X singular when features are collinear or rank-deficient (the inverse does not exist); OLS cannot fit error-prediction points well under actual conditions, which is why the paper introduces local linear weighting (p.6, step 8). Source defects: retracted (peer review compromised, p.1); notation chi reused for both 'dimension vector' (eq 9) and 'ith image feature' (eq 10); empirical accuracy tables unusable.
timescales: tau_3: season-long performance-prediction horizon the system targets

layer2.mapping: The normal equation is the orthogonal projection of a target Y onto the column space of a design matrix X. In the 22-player football dynamical system this is the linear readout that maps observable pre-snap formation/coverage features (X) to a predicted outcome (Y), e.g. expected yards from alignment; lambda_i are the learned tendency coefficients. Collinearity (singular X^T X) is the analogue of aliased formation features that carry no independent information.
layer2.telemetry: In a valid deployment: realized play outcome versus OLS-predicted outcome, and the condition number of X^T X as a collinearity diagnostic. The retracted paper's Tables 1-2 accuracy figures are NOT usable calibration (peer review compromised, p.1); kernel identifiability rests on the formula itself, not on this source's experiments.

primitives.name: Locally weighted least squares with Gaussian kernel (local linear weighting)
primitives.verbatim_quote: For this reason, the local linear weighting method is introduced for analysis, and each predic- tion point is given a certain weight near the area to be predicted
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v_hat: weighted regression coefficient vector [Y/X units]; psi: diagonal weight matrix [dimensionless weights]; X: design matrix [feature units]; Y: target vector [Y units]; w: Gaussian kernel weight [dimensionless, in (0,1]]; x: query point and x^T: reference point [feature units]; ||x^T - x||^2: squared distance [feature units squared]; vartheta: bandwidth parameter [units chosen so the exponent is dimensionless, i.e. 2*v_hat^2*vartheta must carry the same units as ||x^T-x||^2]. The exponent of exp must be dimensionless; this is the dimensional homogeneity constraint. Source eq (17) (WLS) and eq (18) (Gaussian kernel); the exact denominator of eq (18) is garbled by PDF extraction and is transcribed here in the standard Gaussian/LOWESS form, flagged as a transcription uncertainty.
primitives.assumptions: Each prediction point near the area to be predicted receives a weight; a Gaussian kernel supplies the weights with a single bandwidth parameter vartheta; vartheta is set by kernel-function geometry/geometric distance rather than cross-validation to handle large samples (p.7). RETRACTED SOURCE: the journal retracted this article 'due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised' (Retraction notice, PDF p.1; Hindawi Research Integrity investigation). The mathematical kernels below are standard, durable formulas that survive the retraction, but the paper's empirical claims (Tables 1-2, ~80-97% accuracy) are NOT trustworthy and must never calibrate a model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: psi singular or X^T psi X singular makes the weighted inverse undefined; vartheta -> 0 collapses weight onto the nearest point (overfit), vartheta -> infinity degenerates to ordinary least squares (underfit). The source's eq (18) denominator is garbled and its bandwidth-selection claim is unvalidated; retracted source (p.1) means no empirical calibration is trustworthy.
timescales: tau_0: one prediction point and its local neighborhood
tau_1: a local weighted fit at one query
tau_2: bandwidth selection across the sample
tau_3: temporal/spatial performance prediction over a training cycle

layer2.mapping: Locally weighted regression is isomorphic to situation-dependent play-calling: the Gaussian kernel weights recent or similar game situations more heavily, and the bandwidth vartheta is the 'situation similarity' scale (down/distance/field-zone). A coordinator effectively runs a local linear readout whose kernel concentrates on the most relevant prior snaps, exactly as WLS concentrates on nearby points; bandwidth selection is the bias-variance tradeoff between overfitting one tendency and averaging over irrelevant situations.
layer2.telemetry: Per-situation realized outcomes weighted by the kernel; the bandwidth vartheta and the effective sample size (sum of weights). The retracted source supplies no trustworthy bandwidth calibration, so empirical calibration is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from this paper; the kernel form is identifiable from the formula.

primitives.name: Convolutional neural network back-propagation error function (sum of squared outputs)
primitives.verbatim_quote: process, which uses the error function for back-propagation and adjusts the parameters
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E: error function [squared units of w and s]; w^n_k: kth output label corresponding to the nth training sample [label/activation units]; s^n_k: kth network computed value for the nth sample [same units as w]; 1/2: dimensionless constant; the double sum runs over training samples n and outputs k [dimensionless counts]. Dimensional check: (w - s)^2 requires w and s to share units, so E is in those units squared; homogeneous. Source eq (7). NOTE: the source prints both upper limits as m while the prose distinguishes n = number of training samples and k = number of outputs; this is a source notation inconsistency, flagged.
primitives.assumptions: Training is a back-propagation process using the error function to adjust parameters until the maximum number of iterations is reached; output labels and network values are on a common scale; upsampling is required to make front/back layer sizes consistent during error transfer (p.4). RETRACTED SOURCE: the journal retracted this article 'due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised' (Retraction notice, PDF p.1; Hindawi Research Integrity investigation). The mathematical kernels below are standard, durable formulas that survive the retraction, but the paper's empirical claims (Tables 1-2, ~80-97% accuracy) are NOT trustworthy and must never calibrate a model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If labels w and computed values s are not on a common scale the squared difference is dimensionally meaningless; the source reuses m as both summation limits despite distinguishing sample count and output count (notation defect); convergence is to a local minimum, not guaranteed global. Retracted source (p.1): reported recognition accuracy (Table 1) is not usable evidence.
timescales: tau_0: one forward/backward pass on a sample
tau_2: training to the maximum iteration count

layer2.mapping: The sum-of-squares error is the loss whose gradient drives back-propagation; it is isomorphic to the prediction-error signal that updates an internal model of an opponent. In the 22-player system the discrepancy between expected and realized outcomes (w - s) is the teaching signal that adapts tendency weights, and the 1/2-squared form gives a gradient proportional to the error, exactly the prediction-error drive of an adaptive coordinator model.
layer2.telemetry: Training loss E versus iteration and realized pose-estimation error on a held-out set in a valid deployment. The retracted source's Table 1 recognition accuracy (~91-97%) is NOT usable; empirical calibration is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from this paper.

primitives.name: Weighted multi-classifier ensemble fusion rules with information-gain weights
primitives.verbatim_quote: Therefore, this paper gives a certain classiﬁcation weight to each classiﬁer and designs a more comprehensive integration rule
primitives.latex: G_{c_j}=\max_{1\le i\le 5}(Careai\cdot P_{ij}),\quad G_{c_j}=\prod_{i=1}^{5}(Careai\cdot P_{ij}),\quad G_{c_j}=\sum_{1\le i\le 5}(Careai\cdot P_{ij}),\quad Careai=e^{Gain(Z)}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G_cj: fused score for class c_j [probability-like, dimensionless]; P_ij: probability that classifier i assigns class j [probability measure, 0..1]; Careai: weight of the ith classifier [dimensionless, = e^{Gain(Z)}]; Gain(Z): gain value of attribute feature Z [nats, so e^{Gain(Z)} is dimensionless]; Z: feature value of the image classification attribute [feature units]; i indexes the 5 base classifiers [count]; j indexes the m classes [count]. Max, product, and sum of dimensionless weighted probabilities are dimensionless; homogeneous. Source eqs (1)-(5) (fusion rules) and (6) (weight). NOTE: source eqs (1) and (2) are printed IDENTICALLY (both max); eq (4) is count_{1<=i<=5}(P_ij) x argmax(Careai*P_ij). The duplicate is a source defect, flagged.
primitives.assumptions: Five base classifiers; each classifier i has weight Careai and class probability P_ij; the dataset D_i has m categories with class labels C; weights are computed as e^{Gain(Z)} from an attribute feature gain; the five integration rules combine classifier outputs (p.4). RETRACTED SOURCE: the journal retracted this article 'due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised' (Retraction notice, PDF p.1; Hindawi Research Integrity investigation). The mathematical kernels below are standard, durable formulas that survive the retraction, but the paper's empirical claims (Tables 1-2, ~80-97% accuracy) are NOT trustworthy and must never calibrate a model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Source eqs (1) and (2) are identical (both max), an internal inconsistency signaling low editorial rigor; the product rule underflows for many classifiers; Careai = e^{Gain(Z)} can explode without normalization if Gain(Z) is large; P_ij must be calibrated probabilities or the fusion is meaningless. Retracted source (p.1): the fusion's reported accuracy is not trustworthy.
timescales: tau_1: one fusion over the 5 classifiers
tau_3: region classification feeding performance prediction

layer2.mapping: Weighted classifier fusion is isomorphic to combining multiple scouting reports or coverage reads with reliability weights: Careai = e^{Gain(Z)} is an information-gain weighting that trusts the more informative source, and the max/product/sum rules are distinct decision-fusion policies (trust the most confident, require consensus, or pool evidence). In the 22-player system this is how a coordinator aggregates competing reads of the same formation into a single call.
layer2.telemetry: Per-classifier reliability weights and fused-decision accuracy on validated data. Because the source duplicates eqs (1)=(2) and is retracted, its fusion accuracy is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE; only the fusion algebra is identifiable from the formulas.

reasoning_traces.think: The first task with this source is to separate the durable kernel from the disposable narrative, because the article is retracted. The retraction notice on PDF page 1 states the journal retracted the paper 'due to concerns that the peer review process has been compromised' after a Hindawi Research Integrity investigation. That single sentence is the most important invariant in the document: it tells us the empirical channel is corrupted even where the mathematics is sound. The mathematics itself is largely standard. Equation (14) is the ordinary least-squares normal equation lambda = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T Y, a classical projection that predates this paper by two centuries and survives any retraction. Equation (17) is weighted least squares, and equation (18) is a Gaussian kernel; together they are locally weighted regression. Equation (7) is a sum-of-squares training loss. These are legitimate source invariants and can be extracted with full dimensional ledgers. But sovereign rigor demands we also read the defects as evidence. Equations (1) and (2) are printed identically, both as a max over Careai*Pij. The symbol chi is reused for 'dimension vector' in equation (9) and 'ith image feature' in equation (10). The related-work section is about video-surveillance generations and JPEG2000 compression, and the conclusion wanders into household robots, neither of which connects to the sports-training claim. The experimental Tables 1 and 2 report recognition and forecast accuracies between roughly 80 and 97 percent with no baseline, no uncertainty, and no method detail. Read together, these are the signature of a paper-mill artifact: plausible-looking formulas wrapped around an incoherent narrative and unvalidated numbers. Now bind the surviving kernels to the 22-player dynamical system. The normal equation is the linear readout from pre-snap formation features X to a predicted outcome Y; its breakdown, a singular X^T X, is exactly the case of aliased formation features that carry no independent information. Locally weighted regression is situation-dependent play-calling: the Gaussian bandwidth vartheta is the situation-similarity scale, concentrating the readout on the most relevant prior snaps, and the bias-variance tradeoff in choosing vartheta is the tradeoff between overfitting one tendency and averaging over irrelevant situations. The sum-of-squares loss is the prediction-error teaching signal that adapts an internal opponent model. The cross-layer veto is decisive and is the real lesson of this book. The research-integrity layer vetoes the empirical claims even though the mathematical layer is individually valid. A naive extractor would see many equations and high reported accuracy and treat this as a high-value source; the integrity layer says the accuracy tables cannot calibrate anything because the peer-review channel was compromised. So we keep the kernels as source invariants, mark their empirical calibration LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from this source, and refuse to let the retracted numbers seed any downstream model. The invariant survives; the evidence does not.

The durable kernels (the least-squares normal equation, weighted least squares, the Gaussian kernel, the sum-of-squares loss) have a clean classical lineage and survive the retraction; the empirical narrative does not. The hidden state is a corrupted evidence channel wrapped around sound mathematics.
